gloss: cover, cover over; clothe; conceal, hide; cover (sin)
summary: To cover: to lay or spread one thing over another so that it is hidden, clothed or overwhelmed. Locusts, quail, a cloud, the waters of the flood and of the sea cover what is under them; a garment covers nakedness; the earth covers spilled blood; the prudent man covers what he knows. Of sin it cuts both ways: the man who covers his own transgressions does not prosper, but the one who confesses is “covered of sin” by Yahweh (Psa 32:1, 5; Pro 28:13), and Paul reads that covering as righteousness reckoned by faith (Rom 4:7). Its nouns are coverings and clothing: the tabernacle's outer covering of skins, the garment a poor man sleeps in. Arabic kasā “clothe”, Syriac ksā and Jewish Aramaic kassī “cover, hide”, and Ugaritic ksy “cover” show the same root.

words.gloss: cover, cover over, overwhelm; clothe; conceal, hide; cover (sin)
words.summary: About 150 times, nearly all in the piel; the qal has only participles, and the niphal, pual and hithpael are its passives and reflexive. What is covered is out of sight: so the verb runs from spreading over (locusts, cloud, waters) to clothing (nakedness) to concealing (a matter, blood, sin). Its opposite is גָּלָה “uncover, reveal”. The brief's two verb tokens with no stem (Num 4:6, 14) are the noun כְּסוּי, filed here by spelling.

senses.definition: The active participle of the prudent man who keeps to himself what the fool makes known: his knowledge, an insult done him.

evidence.note: “A fool's vexation is known (יִוָּדַע) the same day, וְכֹסֶה קָלוֹן עָרוּם: but the prudent covers an insult.”
“A prudent man כֹּסֶה דָּעַת, but the heart of fools proclaims folly.”

senses.definition: The passive participle in David's blessing: the man whose sin is covered is the man whose transgression is lifted away, forgiven; the next verse says it is the man to whom Yahweh does not reckon iniquity.

evidence.note: “Happy is he whose transgression is lifted (נְשׂוּי־פֶּשַׁע), כְּסוּי חֲטָאָה, covered of sin.”
“Happy the man to whom Yahweh does not reckon iniquity.”
Paul quotes Psa 32:1–2 of righteousness reckoned without works: “whose sins are covered (ἐπεκαλύφθησαν)”; the Peshitta has the ethpaal of ܟܣܐ.

senses.definition: Of a city overwhelmed by the sea, and of blood left on bare rock, uncovered.

evidence.note: “The sea has come up over Babylon; with the roar of its waves נִכְסָתָה.”
Her blood set on the bare rock “לְבִלְתִּי הִכָּסוֹת, that it should not be covered”.

senses.definition: Of hatred hidden by deceit, which is uncovered in the end.

evidence.note: “Hatred תִּכַּסֶּה by guile; its evil תִּגָּלֶה, is uncovered, in the assembly.”

stems.gloss: cover, spread over; overwhelm; clothe; conceal, hide; cover (sin); shelter

senses.definition: To lie or be spread over a thing so that it is no longer seen: locusts over the ground, quail over the camp, fat over the entrails, a network over the capitals, curtains and skins over the tabernacle and its vessels, earth over a pit or excrement.

evidence.note: The locusts “וְכִסָּה אֶת־עֵין הָאָרֶץ, and one will not be able to see the earth”.
The frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
The quail came up וַתְּכַס אֶת־הַמַּחֲנֶה.
“The fat הַמְכַסֶּה אֶת־הַקֶּרֶב, that covers the entrails.”
The network to cover the capitals of the pillars.
The overhang of the curtains on the sides of the tabernacle, to cover it.
The veil of the screen covers the ark of the testimony when the camp sets out.
A man who digs a pit and does not cover it.
Dig with the spade “and cover what comes from you”.
“Covering the altar of Yahweh with tears.”
Who covers the heavens with clouds.
“Darkness יְכַסֶּה־אֶרֶץ, but upon you Yahweh will rise.”
Yahweh has closed the prophets' eyes “and covered your heads, the seers”: the blindness Paul cites in Rom 11:8.
Gog comes up against Israel “like a cloud לְכַסּוֹת הָאָרֶץ” in the latter days: the northern invasion covering the land.

senses.definition: The cloud of Yahweh's glory covering Sinai and the tent of meeting, the sign of his presence on it.

evidence.note: Moses went up “וַיְכַס הֶעָנָן אֶת־הָהָר”.
“The glory of Yahweh dwelt on Mount Sinai, וַיְכַסֵּהוּ הֶעָנָן six days.”
“The cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of Yahweh filled the tabernacle.”
When the congregation gathered against Moses and Aaron, the cloud covered the tent.
A cloud received Jesus out of their sight; the Peshitta has the ethpaal of ܟܣܐ, “he was covered”.

senses.definition: Waters spread over land or sea bed: the deep that covered the earth at its making, which Yahweh bounded so that it will not return to cover the earth, and the waters that cover the sea, the picture of the knowledge of Yahweh filling the earth.

evidence.note: “The deep, as a garment, כִּסִּיתוֹ; the waters stood above the mountains.”
“You set a bound they may not pass, that they not return לְכַסּוֹת הָאָרֶץ.”
“The earth will be full of the knowledge of Yahweh כַּמַּיִם לַיָּם מְכַסִּים, as the waters cover the sea.”
“An abundance of waters covers you.”

senses.definition: To cover over people so that they perish: the sea over Pharaoh's army, the earth over Dathan and Abiram, the deep over Tyre; those under judgment call on the mountains to cover them.

evidence.note: “The waters returned וַיְכַסּוּ the chariots and horsemen … not one of them remained.”
“The depths יְכַסְיֻמוּ; they went down into the deeps like a stone.”
They went down alive to the grave “וַתְּכַס עֲלֵיהֶם הָאָרֶץ, and they perished”.
“When I bring up the deep over you and the great waters cover you.”
“They will say to the mountains, כַּסּוּנוּ, cover us, and to the hills, fall on us.”
Jesus applies Hos 10:8 to the days coming on Jerusalem: “to the hills, cover us (καλύψατε)”; the Peshitta has the pael of ܟܣܐ.

senses.definition: Shame, reproach, horror or violence come over a person like a garment or a flood, so that it is all that is seen of him.

evidence.note: “For the violence to your brother Jacob, shame תְּכַסְּךָ, and you will be cut off for ever.”
“Let us lie down in our shame, and let our reproach cover us, for we have sinned against Yahweh.”
“For your sake I have borne reproach; כִּסְּתָה כְלִמָּה פָנָי.”
“Horror has covered me.”
“The violence of Lebanon will cover you.”

senses.definition: To put a garment over the body, above all over nakedness; to clothe the naked, a righteous man's act. Also of a veil over the face and of the seraphim covering face and feet with their wings.

evidence.note: Shem and Japheth walked backward “וַיְכַסּוּ אֵת עֶרְוַת אֲבִיהֶם”, and did not see it.
Linen breeches “לְכַסּוֹת בְּשַׂר עֶרְוָה”.
“When you see the naked, וְכִסִּיתוֹ.”
The righteous man “covers the naked with a garment”.
King David was old “and they covered him with garments, but he was not warm”.
Yahweh spread his wing over Jerusalem “וָאֲכַסֶּה עֶרְוָתֵךְ” and entered a covenant with her.
Parallel to וָאַלְבִּישֵׁךְ “I clothed you”.
“My wool and my flax, לְכַסּוֹת אֶת־עֶרְוָתָהּ.”
Tassels on “your covering (כְּסוּתְךָ) אֲשֶׁר תְּכַסֶּה־בָּהּ”.
The king of Nineveh covered himself with sackcloth.
Judah took her for a harlot “for she had covered her face”.
“With two he covered his face, and with two he covered his feet.”
“I was naked and you clothed me (περιεβάλετε)”: the act of Isa 58:7 and Ezk 18:7; the Peshitta has the pael of ܟܣܐ.

senses.definition: To keep a thing from being known: a plan, a secret, a deed, or what one ought to declare. Its opposite is גָּלָה “uncover, reveal”.

evidence.note: “הַמְכַסֶּה אֲנִי מֵאַבְרָהָם, shall I hide from Abraham what I am doing?”
“A talebearer מְגַלֶּה סוֹד, reveals a secret, but the faithful of spirit מְכַסֶּה דָבָר.”
“Your righteousness I have not covered within my heart … I have not concealed (כִחַדְתִּי) your חֶסֶד.”
“He who hides hatred has lying lips.”
“The mouth of the wicked covers violence.”
He who puts away his wife “covers his garment with violence”.
“Nothing is covered that will not be revealed”; the Peshitta has ܟܣܐ against ܓܠܐ, the pair of Pro 11:13.

senses.definition: To cover blood with dust so that it no longer cries out: commanded for the blood of game, sought by murderers, and refused by Yahweh to the blood of the slain.

evidence.note: He shall pour out its blood “וְכִסָּהוּ בֶּעָפָר”.
“What profit if we kill our brother וְכִסִּינוּ אֶת־דָּמוֹ?”
She set her blood on the bare rock; she did not pour it on the ground “לְכַסּוֹת עָלָיו עָפָר”.
“O earth, do not cover my blood, and let my cry have no resting place.”
Yahweh comes to punish: “the earth will uncover (וְגִלְּתָה) her blood וְלֹא תְכַסֶּה עוֹד עַל־הֲרוּגֶיהָ”.

senses.definition: With sin or transgression as object. A man covering his own sin hides it from confession, and does not prosper; Yahweh covering sin forgives it, beside “lifting” iniquity; love covers another's transgression by not exposing it.

evidence.note: “מְכַסֶּה פְשָׁעָיו will not prosper, but he who confesses and forsakes them will find mercy.”
“I made my sin known to you, וַעֲוֺנִי לֹא־כִסִּיתִי … and you lifted the iniquity of my sin.”
“If I covered my transgressions like Adam, hiding (לִטְמוֹן) my iniquity in my bosom.”
“You lifted the iniquity of your people; כִּסִּיתָ כָל־חַטָּאתָם.”
“Do not cover their iniquity, and let not their sin be blotted out before you.”
“Hatred stirs up strife, but עַל כָּל־פְּשָׁעִים תְּכַסֶּה אַהֲבָה.”
“He who covers a transgression seeks love, but he who repeats a matter separates friends.”
“Love covers (καλύπτει) a multitude of sins”, from Pro 10:12.
He who turns a sinner back “will cover a multitude of sins”.

senses.definition: Of Yahweh covering his servant in the shadow of his hand.

evidence.note: “I have put my words in your mouth, וּבְצֵל יָדִי כִּסִּיתִיךָ.”
“Deliver me from my enemies, Yahweh; אֵלֶיךָ כִסִּתִי”: obscure, perhaps “with you I have hidden myself”.

senses.definition: Of mountains under the flood or a shadow, ground under weeds, windows under panelling.

evidence.note: “The waters prevailed exceedingly on the earth, וַיְכֻסּוּ all the high mountains that are under all the heavens.”
“Fifteen cubits upward the waters prevailed, וַיְכֻסּוּ הֶהָרִים.”
“The mountains were covered with its shadow.”
The sluggard's field: “its face was covered with nettles”.

senses.definition: Of mourners and penitents clothed in sackcloth.

evidence.note: David and the elders, “מְכֻסִּים בַּשַּׂקִּים”, fell on their faces.

senses.definition: Of the stillborn's name, covered in darkness: never known.

evidence.note: “It came in vanity and goes in darkness, וּבַחֹשֶׁךְ שְׁמוֹ יְכֻסֶּה.”

senses.definition: To put a veil or garment over oneself.

evidence.note: Rebekah “took the veil וַתִּתְכָּס”.
Ahijah “was covering himself with a new cloak”.
“Their webs will not become a garment, nor will they cover themselves with their works.”

senses.definition: To put on sackcloth in mourning and repentance before God.

evidence.note: Hezekiah tore his clothes “וַיִּתְכַּס בַּשָּׂק” and went into the house of Yahweh.
“Let man and beast וְיִתְכַּסּוּ שַׂקִּים and cry mightily to God, and turn each from his evil way.”

evidence.locator: Exo.40.34 יְכַס → ἐκάλυψεν; Psa.85.3 כִּסִּיתָ → ἐκάλυψας; Pro.10.12 תְּכַסֶּה → καλύπτει; Hos.10.8 כַּסּוּ → καλύψατε; καλύπτω renders כָּסָה ×41

evidence.note: “Then they will begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us, and to the hills, Cover us (καλύψατε)”: Hos 10:8.
“Love covers a multitude of sins”: Pro 10:12.
He who turns a sinner back “will cover a multitude of sins”.
The boat covered by the waves.
“Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven and whose sins are covered (ἐπεκαλύφθησαν)”: Psa 32:1.

evidence.locator: Deu.22.12 תְּכַסֶּה → περιβάλῃ; Ezk.18.7 יְכַסֶּה → περιβαλεῖ; Ezk.18.16 כִּסָּה → περιέβαλεν

evidence.note: “I was naked and you clothed me (περιεβάλετέ με)”: the righteous man's act of Isa 58:7 and Ezk 18:7.
The soldiers “put around him a purple robe”; the Peshitta has the pael of ܟܣܐ.

parallels.note: “Lift (iniquity)”: covering sin is lifting it away.
“Blot out”: not to cover sin is not to blot it out.

opposites.note: “Confess”: the man who covers his transgressions against the one who confesses them.

phrases.gloss: cover sin: of Yahweh, forgive; of man, conceal it
the fat that covers the entrails (of the offerings)
as the waters cover the sea

senses.definition: The cover laid over a structure: the roof of Noah's ark, and the outer coverings of rams' skins dyed red and of tachash skins over the tent of the tabernacle and its vessels on the march.

evidence.note: “Noah removed מִכְסֵה הַתֵּבָה and looked, and behold, the face of the ground was dry.”
“A covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering of tachash skins above.”

senses.definition: What a person wears to cover the body: a wife's due clothing, the poor man's only covering to sleep in, the garment with tassels; and in figure the sackcloth over the heavens, and the covering Abaddon lacks before God.

evidence.note: “Her food, כְּסוּתָהּ, and her conjugal right he shall not diminish.”
The pledged cloak: “it is כְסוּתוֹ alone, his garment for his skin; in what shall he sleep?”
“They lie naked without clothing, וְאֵין כְּסוּת in the cold.”
“The grave is naked before him, וְאֵין כְּסוּת to Abaddon.”
“I clothe the heavens with blackness and make sackcloth כְּסוּתָם.”

senses.definition: Abimelech's gift to Sarah, a “covering of the eyes” for all who were with her: what covers a wrong done, so that others look away and she stands vindicated.

evidence.note: “It is for you כְּסוּת עֵינַיִם to all who are with you, and before all you are vindicated.”
Hair is given to a woman “for a covering (περιβολαίου)”; the Peshitta has ܬܟܣܝܬܐ.
“As a garment (περιβόλαιον) you will roll them up”, from Psa 102.

words.summary: The piel participle used as a noun, “that which covers”.

senses.definition: The fat that covers the entrails of an offering.

evidence.note: “The fat tail, וְהַמְכַסֶּה, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver.”

senses.definition: What covers a person or a ship: fine clothing, a ship's awning of blue and purple, and for the fallen king of Babylon a covering of worms.

evidence.note: Tyre's gain will be for those who dwell before Yahweh, to eat their fill “וְלִמְכַסֶּה עָתִיק”, for fine clothing.
“Blue and purple from the isles of Elishah was מְכַסֵּךְ.”
“Your pride is brought down to the grave … maggots are spread under you, וּמְכַסֶּיךָ תּוֹלֵעָה.”

words.summary: Only twice, in the construct כְּסוּי עוֹר תַּחַשׁ, the tachash-skin covering laid over the ark and the altar for the march. The brief also counts here the qal passive participle of Psa 32:1 (כְּסוּי חֲטָאָה), which belongs to the verb.

senses.definition: The covering of tachash skin put over the ark of the testimony and the altar when the camp sets out.

evidence.note: “They shall put on it כְּסוּי עוֹר תַּחַשׁ and spread over it a cloth all of blue.”

words.summary: Only in Ezk 13:18, 20, of the women prophets in the exile who sewed כְּסָתוֹת on the wrists to “hunt souls”. What they were is not certain: bands bound on the arm, or coverings or cushions (Mishnaic כֶּסֶת is a bolster). The Akkadian kasû “bind” and kasītu “(magical) binding”, at home in Babylonian rituals against witchcraft, fit the context; the link to “cover” is not clear, and the word may belong to an older root “bind” in the same spelling.

senses.definition: Things sewn upon the joints of the hands, which Yahweh will tear from the arms of the women who use them to hunt souls.

evidence.note: “Woe to the women who sew כְּסָתוֹת on all the joints of the hands and make veils for the head of every stature, to hunt souls!”
“I am against כִּסְּתוֹתֵיכֶנָה with which you hunt souls … and I will tear them from your arms.”

words.gloss: cover, hide; clothe; (ethpaal) be covered, be clothed, be hidden
words.summary: The Peshitta's ܟܣܐ, for the Greek καλύπτω, κρύπτω and περιβάλλω: it covers, clothes and hides, as the Hebrew does, and stands against ܓܠܐ “reveal”.

senses.definition: What is covered, and will be revealed.

evidence.note: “There is nothing covered that will not be revealed, nor hidden that will not be known.”

senses.definition: To clothe the naked, and to put a robe on a man.

evidence.note: “I was naked and you clothed me.”
They put a purple robe on him.

senses.definition: The mountains called on to cover those under judgment.

evidence.note: “To the hills, cover us”: Hos 10:8.

senses.definition: To hide a thing from some and reveal it to others; to cover the head in prayer.

evidence.note: “You hid these things from the wise and revealed them to babes.”
A man praying “having his head covered”.
“The mystery hidden from ages and generations.”

stems.gloss: be covered; be clothed; be hidden

senses.definition: Of sins covered by God, quoting Psa 32:1.

evidence.note: “Blessed are those whose sins are forgiven and whose sins are covered.”

senses.definition: To be clothed, of Solomon in his glory, and of what one will wear.

evidence.note: “Not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.”

senses.definition: To be covered over or hidden from sight: a boat by the waves, Jesus by the cloud, the things of peace from Jerusalem's eyes.

evidence.note: The boat was covered by the waves.
“A cloud received him (covered him) from their eyes.”
“Now they are hidden from your eyes.”

senses.definition: A garment or covering for the body.

evidence.note: “Put on your garment and follow me.”
“Having food and covering, with these we shall be content.”
Hair given to a woman for a covering.

senses.definition: What is hidden from men and seen by God, to be brought to light at the judgment; with ܒ, “in secret”.

evidence.note: “In the day when God will judge the hidden things of men by Jesus Christ.”
The Lord “will bring to light the hidden things of darkness”.
“The hidden man of the heart.”
“I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world”, from Psa 78:2.
“That your alms may be in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.”

cognates.note: The Arabic keeps the clothing side of the Hebrew: covering the body. Lane reached ك only in his posthumous supplement, so his article is short.

evidence.note: “A garment”: a simple oblong piece of cloth.
“Having clothing.”
“I invested him with a sword.”

evidence.locator: Hebrew כסה (kasá), etymology; Arabic كسا, كساء, كسوة
evidence.note: Hebrew כסה compared with Arabic كَسَا “to cover”; كسا “to clothe, attire, cover”.

cognates.note: The Peshitta's verb and nouns, recorded as words of the entry: the same three sides as the Hebrew, covering, clothing and hiding.

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums and Talmud. The Targum of Gen 38:15 uses it for Tamar's covered face, and the Talmud for covering the blood of a slaughtered animal, as Lev 17:13.

evidence.locator: K00918, כְּסֵי II (ch.), citing Targ. O. Gen. XXXVIII, 15; Ḥull. 87a (cover the blood); Taan. 25a (ithpa., the sky was not covered)
K00912, כְּסוּתָא (ch.), citing Targ. O. Ex. XXII, 8, 25

doctrine.statement: David says the man is happy “whose transgression is lifted, covered of sin”, “to whom Yahweh does not reckon iniquity” (Psa 32:1–2); and he tells how it came: while he kept silent he wasted away, but “I made my sin known to you, and my iniquity I did not cover … and you lifted the iniquity of my sin” (Psa 32:3–5). The proverb gives the rule: “he who covers his transgressions will not prosper, but he who confesses and forsakes them will find mercy” (Pro 28:13); Job disowns covering his sin “like Adam” (Job 31:33). The psalmist praises Yahweh who “covered all their sin” (Psa 85:3), and Nehemiah asks that the enemies' iniquity not be covered (Neh 3:37). Paul quotes Psa 32:1–2 as the blessing of the man “to whom God reckons righteousness apart from works” (Rom 4:6–8), the righteousness reckoned to Abraham when he believed (Rom 4:3). From the verses: sin is covered by God, not by the sinner; the man who hides it is not forgiven, and the one who confesses it and believes has it covered, not reckoned to him.

At the making of the earth “the deep covered it as a garment; the waters stood above the mountains” until at Yahweh's rebuke they fled to their place, “a bound you set, that they may not pass, that they not return to cover the earth” (Psa 104:6–9). In the flood they did return: “the waters prevailed exceedingly on the earth, and all the high mountains that are under all the heavens were covered”, fifteen cubits deep (Gen 7:19–20), and all flesh died (Gen 7:21–22). Afterward Yahweh swore that “the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh” (Gen 9:11, 15), and Peter writes that “the world that then was, being flooded with water, perished” (2Pe 3:6). From the verses: the flood covered every high mountain under the whole heaven; a flood confined to one region would not cover all the mountains under heaven, and the promise that it will not return to cover the earth answers a flood that covered all of it.

Isaiah sees the shoot from the stump of Jesse, on whom the spirit of Yahweh rests, judge the poor and strike the earth with the rod of his mouth (Isa 11:1–4); then “they will not hurt or destroy in all my holy mountain, for the earth will be full of the knowledge of Yahweh as the waters cover the sea” (Isa 11:9), and the nations will seek the root of Jesse (Isa 11:10), whom Paul names as Christ ruling the Gentiles (Rom 15:12). Habakkuk repeats it: “the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of Yahweh, as the waters cover the sea” (Hab 2:14), as Yahweh swore in the wilderness that “all the earth shall be filled with the glory of Yahweh” (Num 14:21). From the verses: the knowledge and glory of Yahweh will cover the earth itself as completely as water fills the sea bed, under the rule of the son of Jesse; the hope is a kingdom on the earth.

note: Words: the verb (k.cg.aa) and its nouns מִכְסֶה (k.cg.ad, with the zero-token cross-reference m.bx.an), כְּסוּת (k.cg.ac), מְכַסֶּה (k.cg.ae), כְּסוּי (k.cg.ab, with the zero-token k.ch.af), and כֶּסֶת (k.ch.ab, with BDB's second root key k.ch.aa “bind” and the cross-reference k.cm.ad).
